questions.q: Tell me about a digital marketing campaign you worked on. What was the goal, which channels did you use, and what was your part?
questions.looks_for: Real campaign, clear goal (leads, sales, followers), channels like Meta ads, Google ads, SEO, email, their own tasks, and numbers if available.

questions.q: Share a result you are proud of, like more leads or lower cost. What did you change to get that result?
questions.looks_for: Specific metric before and after, and the change made (targeting, creative, keywords, landing page); shows testing and learning.

questions.q: What is the difference between CTR and conversion rate, and which would you watch for a lead generation campaign?
questions.looks_for: CTR is clicks over impressions, conversion rate is actions over clicks/visits; for leads the conversion and cost per lead matter more than CTR alone.

questions.q: How does SEO help a small business, and what are two or three basic things you would check on their website first?
questions.looks_for: Free traffic from search over time; checks page titles and descriptions, speed, mobile view, Google Business Profile, useful content, keywords.

questions.q: When would you use paid ads instead of only organic social media posts?
questions.looks_for: Paid for quick reach, targeting, launches, or offers; organic for trust and community over time; mentions budget and tracking.

questions.q: Your Meta ads campaign spent half the monthly budget in one week but brought very few leads. What would you do?
questions.looks_for: Pauses or reduces weak ads, checks targeting, creatives, form and landing page, looks at data by ad set, tests changes, reports honestly to the manager.

questions.q: Why do you want this digital marketing job, when can you join (state your notice period), and what salary do you expect?
questions.looks_for: Clear reason linked to the work, states notice period or joining date in days or weeks, and gives an expected monthly or yearly salary figure or range without dodging.
